name: Daya Bay
summary: Daya Bay compared reactor-antineutrino rates and spectra in multiple near and far detector halls in southern China. It discovered a nonzero theta13 and delivered a precise measurement of this mixing angle from its full data set.
detection_principle: Nominally identical gadolinium-loaded liquid-scintillator modules identify inverse beta decay using prompt positron light and delayed neutron-capture gamma rays. Near detectors constrain the emitted flux, while far detectors measure oscillation-induced disappearance.
